# Project guide

iCode Teams: a client and release platform for internal enterprise Agent applications. It is a TypeScript ESM monorepo on Node 22+ (CI and test gates are pinned to 24.14.1). The plugin framework is `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, the client UI uses React 19 + antd 6, server storage uses PostgreSQL (`pg`), and observability goes to Control over OpenTelemetry OTLP.

## Directories and ownership boundaries

```text
business/       # Business plugins: domain/<business plugin> (each with its own docs/specs); platform foundation plugins in foundation/ (accounts, auth, teams); shared, tests, third-party
framework/      # Client processes client/{core,daemon,gateway,ui}; service business host service/business-host; shared contracts such as shared/plugin-contracts; docs, tests
console/        # Control management plane: src (single process, single Store), contracts, docs, tests
engineering/    # Release in release/; architecture guards in architecture/ (source-path-map, fallback-exceptions); docs in docs/; tests in tests/ and test support in testing/ (runner, registries)
operations/     # Deployment and installation in applications/deployment (docs, src, install, tests)
observability/  # telemetry (src, contracts) and diagnostics (feature-catalog, etc.); docs
docs/           # Cross-domain docs: architecture/ (cross-domain architecture), product/, specs/ and the README index
```

Module ids are mapped from physical paths by `engineering/architecture/source-path-map.json`. Dependency direction is enforced statically by `engineering/tests/unit/architecture/architecture-boundaries.test.ts`: business plugins do not import host internals, cross-scope imports are forbidden, and plugins depend only on the public contracts of platform plugins. `pg` is allowed only in the business host PG facility; all plugin storage goes through the host PluginDatabase facility. A plugin connecting to PG directly is a registered exception; currently the only one is the data-access direct connection (the `source-boundaries.ts` allowlist, authorized by the maintainers on 2026-10-15). Before changing code, decide which ownership directory a new file belongs in, and keep source-path-map consistent with it.

## Common commands

- `npm run dev`: starts the full local environment: Control (45830) + Service + Daemon/Core (45831) + Gateway (45833). Requires `ICODE_PG_URL` to point to a local PostgreSQL. Console at <http://127.0.0.1:45830>, demo account `admin` / `icode-teams-demo-password`.
- Before committing: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint:ui` (ESLint + style token check), and complete the verification required by the plan from `python3 engineering/testing/test_scope.py --base <fixed PR base>`. Delivery tests excluded from PRs by default are listed in `deferredDeliveryTests`; add `--delivery` for a manual delivery plan. `npm run test:pr` is still the full local entry point including packaging; it is not the same as PR CI.
- `npm test` (integration), `npm run test:e2e` (end-to-end), `npm run test:focus` (single file, must be registered in `engineering/testing/test-targets.json`), `npm run test:fallback` (fallback guard). Non-local tests need `ICODE_TEST_PG_URL`.
- The test runner is the in-house `engineering/testing/run-tests.mjs` (a wrapper around `node:test`). Do not call `node --test` or `vitest`/`jest` directly.

## Test conventions

Every test case must be classified explicitly: business cases use `flowTest`, everything else uses `caseTest` with a `reason`. Do not import the `node:test` registration functions directly. Business assertions must sit inside an `operation.checkpoint(...)` callback; Trace evidence is produced by the production implementation, and tests must not fabricate events. See [Test gates](engineering/docs/testing-gates.md); example: `framework/tests/integration/client/installation/management-flow.test.ts`.

## Coding standards

- ESLint covers only client and plugin source directories. `no-alert` is an error; the two react-hooks rules are legacy allowances, and new code must not rely on them (`eslint.config.mjs`).
- Styles: raw hex colors are forbidden (`npm run lint:style` fails hard). Always use `--ui-*` CSS variables and keep both themes complete. Data requests go through `tracedFetch`/`tracedJson`; raw fetch is forbidden. Use only antd; plugin UI goes through the `framework/client/ui/src/contracts/ui.ts` contract. See [Frontend common style guide](engineering/docs/frontend-common-style-guide.md).
- All persistence uses an atomic flush+rename commit. Failures must be explicit; an explicit failure is better than a silent fallback.

## Do not edit by hand

- `observability/diagnostics/src/feature-catalog.generated.ts`: generated by `engineering/testing/feature-catalog.ts`.
- Registries protected by fingerprints/contracts, where changes have knock-on effects: `engineering/release/release-components.json` (part of the incremental release fingerprint), `engineering/testing/test-targets.json`, `engineering/testing/control-test-scopes.json`, `engineering/architecture/fallback-exceptions.json`.
- `coverage/`, `dist/` and `.demo-data/` are output directories; do not commit them.

For the detailed development flow (installation, packaging, rolling out upgrades), see the [README](README.md) and the [documentation index](docs/README.md).

# Project constraints

## Fallbacks are forbidden by default

- Unless explicitly requested, do not add or widen fallbacks, silently swallowed errors, alternative data sources, alternative implementations or legacy protocol compatibility paths.
- Exceptions may be proposed only for an explicit requirement or a failure exposed by real users / real tests. First explain why the root cause cannot be fixed, then confirm the allowed trigger conditions. Do not invent requirements for your own implementation.
- Normal default configuration, handling ENOENT on first installation as the contract requires, explicit failures and necessary cleanup are not fallbacks. Do not treat corruption, permission errors or network failures as "does not exist".
- An exception must record the real scenario it is based on, the reason for keeping it and a regression test. The test must prove the behavior under the specified failure and show that other failures are not masked. Adding or widening an exception requires explicit confirmation from the user / maintainers; it cannot be authorized just by writing your own comments or tests.
- Detailed rules and handling of existing cases: `engineering/docs/fallback-policy.md`.

## Project-level common gate checks

Developer self-checks and committor checks both use the repository's [architecture-self-check Skill](.agents/skills/architecture-self-check/SKILL.md). Use it when the user asks for a common check, a pre-commit self-check, a commit, a push, or creating or updating a PR; do not rely on personal Skills. The flow is: review the changes, find issues, report results. For detailed dimensions and evidence boundaries, see the [common check guide](engineering/docs/pr-self-check.md).

The Skill only checks and reports. It does not modify the code, tests or rules under review, does not fix anything, does not approve exceptions or decide merges, and does not widen commit or release permissions. It reuses the full required PR plan and valid evidence from [Test gates](engineering/docs/testing-gates.md); missing verification must not be treated as passing. Changes to the checkers, shared test cases, exception registries and trigger rules themselves must be shown to the committor; protection must not be weakened to clear a failure. Having the Skill does not mean CI or branch protection blocking is enabled.

## Documentation and process output

- The repository maintains only current standards, active designs, test code and necessary decisions / authorization conditions; see the [documentation maintenance rules](./docs/README.md) for the detailed categories.
- Self-check conclusions, implementation progress and delivery summaries go into the current reply or the PR description; do not create process documents in the repository. Logs, screenshots and raw measurements go to a temporary directory outside the repository or an existing ignored output directory; CI uses artifacts.
- Do not create docs/history/ or docs/development/evidence/. New long-lived documents must go into the agreed topic directories and be reachable from the documentation index. A Spec states its status, scope and owner role; once complete, extract the conclusions and delete the process drafts.
- Run the documentation checks in the required plan before committing. Changes to checkers or governance rules must state the reason and the change in protection in the PR; rules must not be loosened to clear a failure. Co-located material such as Skills and test fixtures follows the maintenance rules.

# iCode Teams A client and release platform for internal enterprise Agent applications. It includes the client, the server control plane (Control), the server business plane (Service/Business) and independently upgradable plugins. [Development guide](#development-guide) · [Optional npm plugins](#optional-npm-plugins) · [Local source debugging](#local-source-debugging) · [Documentation index](./docs/README.md) ## Development guide Day-to-day development order: install a test client → change code and build an incremental package → roll out the upgrade from the console → verify the feature. | Entry | Purpose | | --- | --- | | [Test console](https://teams-test-helloicode.duckdns.org/) | Sign in, view devices, publish components and check deployment results; both the client control service and the business service use this address | | [Shared artifact registry](https://teams-registry-helloicode.duckdns.org/npm-v2/) | Stores test/prod artifacts; `package:release` publishes here by default | Before you start, ask the environment maintainers for a test account, the deployment permissions you need and GitHub Actions publishing permission. Day-to-day development reuses the existing servers. For full packaging, server installation and environment configuration, see the [Packaging and environment deployment guide](operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md). ### First client installation Install once on the device you will test with; later upgrades go through the console. macOS ARM64 / Linux x64: ```bash curl -fsSL https://teams-test-helloicode.duckdns.org/install.sh -o /tmp/icode-teams-install.sh && \ sh /tmp/icode-teams-install.sh --profile test --server https://teams-test-helloicode.duckdns.org ``` Windows x64: first run `whoami /user` in the Windows user session that will use the client and note the SID. Then run the following in an administrator PowerShell for the same user, replacing the example SID with the real value: ```powershell $installer = "$env:TEMP\icode-teams-install.ps1" Invoke-WebRequest https://teams-test-helloicode.duckdns.org/install.ps1 -OutFile $installer -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $installer -TargetUserSid 'S-1-5-21-111-222-333-1001' -Profile test -ServerUrl https://teams-test-helloicode.duckdns.org ``` Installation does not need a token. After you open the client and sign in with the test account, the device registers and binds automatically. On the "Clients" page of the [test console](https://teams-test-helloicode.duckdns.org/), confirm that your device is online and note its device name or ID; later upgrades should select only your own test device. For the production environment, custom directories, reinstalling and start/stop commands, see [Client installation and upgrade](framework/client/docs/client-installation.md). ### Incremental packaging Development and packaging commands use Node.js 24.14.1. The first time, install dependencies in the repository root and sign in to the GitHub CLI: ```bash npm ci --no-audit gh auth login ``` Finish the code changes and the necessary checks, push the commits to a remote development branch, then run in the repository root: ```bash npm run package:release -- --ref --channel test --scope components ``` Replace `` with the actual branch name; for merged code you can use `main`. The command uses the remote commit, assigns versions automatically, builds only changed components and reuses unchanged artifacts. By default it waits for Actions to finish and prints the npm publishing result. After packaging succeeds you still need to roll out the upgrade. Test builds automatically use the original GitHub release run ID as the `-test.N` number. To publish only one component, replace the scope with the component ID, for example `control-host`; separate multiple components with commas. Use incremental publishing when only plugins or Hosts change; changes to the installer, Compose or the updater require a full package, deployed by the environment maintainers. Production packaging uses `npm run package:release -- --ref main --channel prod --scope all`; versions are read from `engineering/release/versions.json` at that fixed source commit. The main integration environment verifies production candidates with an explicit release number through the [Main integration workflow](operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md#main-integration-workflow). The release and all Teams members must use production versions without a prerelease suffix; prod reuses the same candidate's versions and artifacts after acceptance and promotion. `channel` determines how release versions are assigned; the deployment `environment` determines the target configuration and data isolation. The `test` installation profile underneath main is used only for environment isolation. Test versions cannot be main/prod candidates, and production versions still need admission to the corresponding environment. The registry is deployed independently, and the release catalog and installation packages all use npm. For configuration and first deployment, see the [Packaging and deployment guide](operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md). If you stop waiting, you can continue querying the same packaging run with the printed run ID: ```bash npm run package:release -- --run-id ``` ### Roll out upgrades Confirm that Actions has finished packaging, then sign in to the [test console](https://teams-test-helloicode.duckdns.org/) and click "Refresh" at the top to read the release catalog. On the "Clients" page, find your test device by device name or ID, confirm it is online, select it and click "Batch upgrade". | Upgrade mode | When to use | | --- | --- | | All client components | Update the selected test devices as a whole; Control plans target versions and matching dependencies from the release catalog | | Single client component | Target only one client component or Teams plugin; select the component and target version | | Component combination | Target several components, new plugins or a cross-end combination; select the components taking part and choose a version for each | 1. Click "Generate upgrade preview" and check the target devices, the components actually involved, versions, matching dependencies and restart impact. If anything is blocking, resolve the cause first and preview again. 2. "Execution mode" defaults to "Each device runs independently (default)". After you click "Start preparing this plan", each ordinary client can switch as soon as its preparation completes, without waiting for the whole batch; actual Service dependencies are still ordered by the plan. 3. If you choose "Admin confirms the switch after preparation", go to the "Server" page, open "View details" for the task, and click "Confirm switch" once preparation is complete. 4. **Upgrades that include Core also need local confirmation on the client by default.** When the client shows "Client update ready", save your edits first, then click "Refresh and update". This is a separate confirmation step from Control's "Confirm switch". 5. On the Control "Server" page, check the upgrade task and device details to confirm the upgrade actually completed. Then go back to the "Clients" page to check the actual version, health status and Desired / Actual convergence, and run the functional verification for this change. Offline devices continue with the original plan once they come online; a task being accepted or prepared does not mean the upgrade succeeded. For server plugins or Hosts that are already installed, select the target version on the "Server" page, click "Preview upgrade", then follow the same preview, preparation and execution steps. Control Host and Business Host are selected independently; matching components follow the real dependencies and the Host API validation results. New server plugins can also be added through "Select components" on the "Component release" page. "Select components" on the "Component release" page selects all clients by default. When a test release involves clients, narrow down the devices on the "Clients" page first. The servers are shared by the team; coordinate with the environment maintainers before upgrading them. For canary, online acceptance and rollback rules for cross-end releases, see [End-to-end release](./docs/architecture/end-to-end-feature-release.md). ### Upgrade clients with the Control CLI Use the standalone management command `icode-teams-control`; it needs a Control administrator account. The examples below run in Bash on macOS / Linux; finish packaging before you start. Run the preparation script, which automatically fetches the latest CLI from the release catalog; an installed copy of the same version that passes verification is reused. - The author of a change updates the affected behavior, commands, configuration and interface descriptions in the same PR, reviewed by the corresponding module or business Owner. Do not change dates mechanically when behavior has not changed.
- Check this index first and prefer editing an existing authoritative document. When adding a document, add it to the owning index and state its audience and lifecycle.

- When closing a Spec, move the stable conclusions into the standards and point remaining work to an Issue/to-do or a short to-be-verified list for the topic; process records stay in Git/PR. ## Documentation change checks

Check relative file links and anchors, whether npm commands for this repository are still in package.json, whether current standards still contain superseded statements, and whether new pages have an index entry. Historical originals stay in Git/PR and are judged against their own baseline.

Run `python3 engineering/architecture/docs.py` in the repository root. It checks Markdown in the root README, the top-level docs/ and the module docs registered in `MODULE_DOC_ROOTS`: relative file links, Markdown/HTML anchors and npm commands in current guides. It supports inline links, images and reference link definitions, ATX/Setext headings and HTML id/name. Link examples inside code fences are not checked, and example commands are checked by name only, not executed. Inline code, source paths in code examples, command arguments and semantic consistency between sections still need manual review.

Every `npm run` in current guides is treated as a command of this repository. External URL availability, HTML snapshot bodies, full CommonMark syntax and whether the content matches the implementation are outside what this check guarantees and still need review. Whether design statuses and Owners are accurate also needs manual verification.

The documentation check is part of the required plan and runs for both documentation-only and code changes. The CI result fingerprint includes the documentation and the repository link targets, so stale successful runs are not reused. `python3 engineering/tests/unit/architecture/test_docs.py` verifies the checker's behavior and is selected by the required plan when the checker changes. The original architecture-boundaries protection of specific architecture statements is kept. Test selection follows [Test gates](../engineering/docs/testing-gates.md); documentation-only changes do not start unrelated business or platform installation tests.

## Automatic structure gates

The documentation check covers the whole candidate worktree: CI checks the candidate commit, and locally it also includes staged, unstaged and new unignored files; it does not check only the last push. The rules are:

- No files of any kind, including non-Markdown artifacts, under docs/history/, docs/development/evidence/, or history/evidence directories in registered module docs.
- Cross-module docs live in the architecture, development, deployment, product or specs topic directories under docs; the docs root keeps only README.md. Module docs live in paths explicitly registered in `MODULE_DOC_ROOTS` of the [checker](../engineering/architecture/docs.py); the six top-level directories are not allowed wholesale. Documents must be reachable from the root README and docs/README.md through real Markdown file links; orphan pages or orphan cycles fail. HTML can be an index target, but a snapshot's internal navigation does not prove it is in the current index.
- The repository root allows only README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, SECURITY.md and LICENSE.md. Outside the documentation directories above, Markdown/RST is allowed only for co-located README/AGENTS files, Skill material under .agents/skills, and fixtures/prompts/templates material under tests. Any other document read by a program must be justified in the rule change with valid/invalid regressions added; exemptions are not widened silently.
- Everything in specs except the directory README uses Markdown. Top-level Specs must be reachable from docs/specs/README.md, and module Specs from their module's docs/specs/README.md, while also meeting the global reachability requirement from the root README and docs/README.md. Each Spec has one non-empty field each: `- Status:`, `- Scope:`, `- Owner role:`. Status is only "in discussion", "in implementation" or "to be verified"; distill the conclusions of completed or abandoned designs and then remove them. The owner role can be a maintenance role; if nobody has claimed it yet, say so honestly.

The checker does not infer a document's purpose from words like "report" or "progress". It cannot recognize process drafts disguised as standards, and it cannot prove that statuses and owner roles are accurate. Content still needs review; changes to structure rules and the checker must state the change in protection and get focused review from the maintainers. A CI failure makes local-gate fail; whether it blocks merging depends on whether the repository's branch rules make that status a required check. Local configuration does not mean the remote rule is enabled.

# Project-level common gate check

This Skill keeps the `architecture-self-check` name and path as the single common Skill; the framework and plugins use the same entry point and do not rely on personally installed Skills. It guards the framework and common logic; business domain rules are left to dedicated reviews. For detailed rules see the [common check guide](../../../engineering/docs/pr-self-check.md), and read the relevant authoritative standards for the change.

Identity isolation, data integrity, completion conditions, permissions and resource lifecycle are common correctness concerns and must be checked even when the implementation is in a business plugin. Product strategy and scenarios not declared as supported are still for the business Owner to judge.

When the task explicitly asks to focus on P0/P1, prioritize tracing paths that could cause severe functional failure, data corruption or loss, privilege escalation or runaway resources; for architecture issues, state the concrete severe consequence. Report only P0/P1 findings with sufficient evidence. Do not expand on refactoring, style or documentation suggestions already known to be P2/P3, and do not inflate severity to pad the number of findings. Still cover the whole candidate diff and briefly keep the protection changes, actual coverage and verification gaps; no high-priority findings does not mean verification passed. When no severity range is given, run the full common check.

This Skill only checks and reports. It does not modify the code, tests or rules under review, does not develop checkers, does not approve fallback exceptions and does not decide merges. Fixing is a separate development task; this entry point does not authorize staging, committing, pushing, creating PRs, deploying or touching real installations. Having the Skill does not mean CI or branch protection blocking is enabled.

## 1. Review the changes

Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md), git status, the full candidate diff and the necessary context. A base specified by the user takes priority; for an existing PR, use the merge-base with the actual base and record the resolved commit. Distinguish committed, staged and unstaged changes and related new unignored files. Be clear whether the target is the committed candidate at the current HEAD or a worktree candidate including uncommitted changes; if the base is unavailable, report the scope gap. Look at both sides and at deleted protections; do not expand this into a whole-repository audit.

Choose from the five common dimensions in the guide: architecture, framework contracts, test organization and trigger scope, exceptions and fallbacks, framework observability integration. Confirming scope, choosing dimensions and verifying evidence are internal steps and do not add step-by-step approvals.

When responsibilities, dependencies, assembly or persistence change, check the boundaries of the six ownership directories, the named assembly entry points and the single state writer against the [current architecture](../../../docs/architecture/overview.md#dependencies-and-state). When a registered public boundary is involved, review the before/after against the [contract, implementation and consumer registry](../../../engineering/architecture/public-boundaries.json). Passing static checks does not replace judging responsibility and state ownership.

## 2. Find issues

Review the candidate's behavior and architecture first, then check the automated evidence. Following [behavior and architecture review](../../../engineering/docs/pr-self-check.md#behavior-and-architecture-review), trace the high-risk paths touched by this change through the real entry point, implementation, state commit and callers; the relevant context may be in unchanged files. Do not treat passing types/scans/existing tests as the boundary of finding issues, and do not exclude common correctness issues just because the code is in a business directory.

Focus by what the change triggers: for cross-layer calls, check the overall budget, permissions and capacity; for async or concurrent code, check request identity, ownership and commit ordering; for pagination and windows, check persisted progress and completion conditions; for recovery and switching, check follow-up operations, restarts and old instances; for new public capabilities, check responsibility, actual consumers and credential flow. Check the paths actually involved; do not expand into a whole-repository audit or a fixed failure matrix for every PR.

From the repository root, run `python3 engineering/testing/test_scope.py --base <fixed PR base>`. Add `--committed` only when checking just the committed candidate at the current HEAD (including in CI); do not add it for pre-commit checks even if all changes are staged, because the option excludes all uncommitted changes. Reuse the required plan, selection reasons, check implementation and valid execution evidence from [Test gates](../../../engineering/docs/testing-gates.md); do not maintain a second set of rules or a full test dependency table. Read the before/after snippets, categories and `gaps` in the plan's `changeFacts`, and verify the impact together with `reasons`; textual clues do not decide whether a contract changed or a protection was weakened. Scope is decided by the plan: changes to AGENTS/Skills are not treated as documentation-only by the existing selectors. The default PR plan excludes delivery tests; check `deferredDeliveryTests`, and do not report a green PR as packaging, deployment or upgrade being verified. When the manual delivery scope needs checking, add `--delivery` explicitly.

When creating, updating or checking a PR, read the actual body or the draft to be published, and check the `ci-validation` required for code PRs according to [PR validation statement](../../../engineering/docs/testing-gates.md#pr-validation-statement). For a committed candidate, run or reuse the existing `ci_evidence.py validate-pr` precheck result; exact scenario names, platforms and actual results are still checked against run evidence. Generating a test plan successfully does not mean the statement passes, and a passing statement does not mean the tests pass; report unpublished statements as drafts.

Check the candidate, base, inputs, run conditions and platform of existing results, and run checks suited to the current environment only for required results that are missing or invalid; do not repeat valid verification. Final admission for an automated PR checks the trusted coordinator's `PR validation result`; success of `PR execution result` and `PR workflow validation` does not replace admission of the current candidate. Code PRs keep all shared protections; expensive verification is chosen by old and new dependency impact. Do not use the diff of the last push to narrow the required scope of the whole PR. If the environment, permissions or capabilities are insufficient, continue with what can run and report the gap; do not replace verification with model reasoning.

Cross-check with existing automated results, behavior test cases and real entry point code. Check whether the related tests actually set up the claimed scenario, and whether the assertions would still pass if the key behavior were wrong or not executed. Where resource or plugin call risks apply, use the [resource scanning tools](../../../engineering/docs/pre-pr-review.md) for extra leads; an incomplete scan is not a pass, and hits need their scenario verified. Keep the location and evidence for each group of hits, and classify them as existing protection / needs a test case / issue found / not applicable. A test existing, no static hits and a passing run each fail to prove uncovered behavior.

If the candidate changes during the check, state which conclusions or evidence are invalidated. Do not claim old results cover the new version, and do not re-check endlessly on your own. Changes to checkers, shared test cases, exception registries and trigger rules must be shown; passing after a change does not mean the original protection may be weakened.

## 3. Report results

In the current reply or a PR description you are authorized to edit, briefly state the base, the candidate, actual coverage and the executed/reused results, then separate:

- Confirmed issues: within the scope specified by the task, mark severity (P0/P1/P2, etc.), location, trigger scenario, root cause, consequence, the established rule violated and the evidence. Distinguish code path evidence, controlled reproduction and real host verification. Severity is based on impact; do not downgrade it just because nothing ran on a real machine, and do not rate missing tests as P1 by default.
- Changes for the committor to review: before/after facts, known impact, reasoning and trade-offs in supported scope; an intentional change to a rule or contract is not automatically a defect.
- Verification gaps: what was not analyzed, not run, failed, partially done or unresolved, and why; do not merge these into "passed".

Group statements by risk; a fixed long report is not required. Automated checks verify established rules; the committor judges whether changes to rules, contracts or architecture are reasonable. Reports and temporary evidence are stored according to the [AGENTS documentation and process output rules](../../../AGENTS.md#documentation-and-process-output); do not create process documents in the repository.

# iCode Teams Control

Use `icode-teams-control` as the supported adapter for Control administrator operations. Preserve the same business semantics as the Web UI; do not reproduce orchestration with lower-level HTTP calls.

Obtain the registry and Control origins from the task's private configuration or existing local contexts. Keep real addresses, credentials and raw output containing them out of repository files and public reports. Respect the requested target; inspect the selected context before remote operations. For the installation examples, set `TEAMS_REGISTRY` from that private input and require it to be nonempty; pass it explicitly to the preparation script.

## Prepare the CLI automatically

At the start of every task using this Skill, run the preparation script from this Skill directory before any Control operation:

```sh
node scripts/install-control-cli.mjs --registry "$TEAMS_REGISTRY"
```

It selects the highest eligible CLI version from the committed publication catalog, reuses a verified local copy or installs it automatically, and returns its absolute `executable` path. Users do not need to choose a version or approve this local tool update. Keep using that returned path throughout the task; installations are isolated by registry and version so another task's update cannot replace it. Stop if preparation fails; do not continue with an older CLI or a source checkout.

Only use `--version <exact-version>` when the task explicitly requests a pinned version; it must also be committed and not withdrawn. If registry authentication is required, use the machine's existing npm configuration. Never place a token in a command argument, repository file, output, or Control context.

## Configure and authenticate

Inspect existing contexts before changing them:

```sh
<cli> contexts list --json
```

Create or update a named context only when the target Control origin and environment are known, then select it explicitly. Control requires HTTPS except for loopback development instances.

```sh
<cli> contexts set <name> --server <https-origin> --environment <environment> --json
<cli> contexts use <name> --json
```

For an interactive administrator login, provide the password only through `ICODE_TEAMS_CONTROL_PASSWORD`; do not write it into command history or messages. Automation should use a Control automation token associated with the recorded actor. Token creation returns the secret once, so do not repeat it in output.

## Choose the deployment route

Use the [delivery map](../../../docs/development/delivery-map.md) for the shared stages and completion conditions. Resolve the requested environment from private configuration, then inspect its actual identity with `<cli> server identity --context <name> --json`. A context name is a local label, not proof of the connected instance.

The map's `test` currently corresponds to instance purpose `dev`; `main` has purpose `main` and server installation profile `main` (runtime deployment environment remains `test`, and release candidates use stable `prod` versions), and `prod` has purpose/channel `prod`. Client bindings retain `profile=test, instance=main`; do not pass the server's profile to the client installer. Existing MAIN server resources under `test` require explicit state-preserving relocation before using the new deployment route.

For TEST end-to-end validation, follow the map's Linux server/registry and native client topology. Confirm the actual TEST configuration and selected devices; a local context label or an isolated CI fixture is not an environment identity. A required independent registry belongs on Linux and must be explicitly connected to the TEST services. Windows test devices run clients, not replacement registries or Control/Business Hosts. Report isolated regression results separately from real TEST deployment and business verification.

| Requested work | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Test an already published branch component | Select its exact published version and intended targets, then use [component deployment](#upgrade-clients-and-components). |
| Prepare or deploy a new main candidate | Follow [main integration](#main-integration); changing the CLI context alone does not bind a new candidate. |
| Promote a main candidate or deploy prod-admitted components | Follow [production deployment](#production-deployment). |
| First installation or full server package/configuration replacement | Follow the [business deployment guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/business-deployment.md); the existing scripts call Control for subsequent component operations. Infrastructure prerequisites belong to that guide. |

If the requested release does not yet exist, use the [publication instructions](../../../README.md#package-release) within the task's authorized source and component scope. This Skill routes to that entry rather than assembling or uploading its own release. Keep missing private configuration or access explicit; do not substitute another environment or enable repository automation as a side effect.

### Main integration

Read the [main integration workflow guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md#main-integration-workflow) and [main preparation and deployment guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/business-deployment.md#main-preparation-and-deployment) for this route.

- MAIN consumes independently archived component manifests from its configured registry. `deploy=true` freezes metadata once; it neither builds a complete combination nor downloads every component. Source/versions/digests stay fixed when main or latest advances. A workflow retry restores its original selection artifact and explicitly fails if that identity is unavailable, ambiguous or withdrawn.
- The common server route is `prepare → plan → apply → verify` through the business deployment adapter. Reuse one task directory, compiled spec and exact published CLI. TEST and MAIN use the same execution contract with different environment inputs. Read actual installed state, stage only needed components, and verify both Hosts, plugins, health, database and effective server configuration. Preserve the local installation hold, original installer recovery and data.
- Client availability, old client tasks and cross-end compatibility inference do not gate server installation. Fixed `mainValidationNodeIds` authorize only a separate dedicated validation task. `environment-validation.ts client` consumes the same frozen manifests and original server deployment ID, upgrades that one bound device through the public CLI and verifies actual component identities and fresh health.
- `environment-validation.ts business` executes developer-specified cases or consumes their explicit operation identities, then verifies real retained cross-end Trace at the selected versions after server deployment. Client and business failures are independent results, not server-install failures. Do not set accepted from a package or server result; preserve historical real acceptance facts.
- Main integration has separate server, client-validation and business-validation jobs; the latter two require their explicit workflow flags/private inputs. Ordinary client rollout remains manual CLI work and is outside this server workflow. New archive-validation receipts do not silently open ordinary selection or grant PROD promotion. Existing accepted-candidate and native acceptance contracts remain authoritative for promotion.
- Follow the current [main deployment guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/business-deployment.md#main-preparation-and-deployment) for task directories, first installation, exact-version input, repeat/recovery and validation commands. Report server deployment, dedicated client validation and developer business results separately, including not-run or failed tasks.

### Production deployment

Use the exact immutable candidate admitted to prod. Follow [environment admission and promotion](../../../engineering/release/docs/release-trust.md#environment-views-and-same-candidate-promotion): the protected `Promote release` workflow verifies the candidate's main acceptance and trusted Linux, Windows and server release acceptance before granting prod eligibility. Version suffixes do not grant eligibility; preserve the candidate's original versions, bytes and artifact references without rebuilding or renaming them. Missing admission or acceptance evidence blocks production deployment.

Follow the [prod candidate deployment guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/business-deployment.md#prod-same-candidate-deployment) to export and bind the selected candidate through private deployment configuration. For a prod instance already bound to that candidate, use the same Control CLI preview/start/wait lifecycle with exact admitted versions. Completion includes actual version/health checks and the requested production business acceptance. Preserve the production Core confirmation requirement. Full server installation/configuration changes use that guide; a successful main run does not itself authorize promotion or production deployment.

## Run operations

- Prefer `--json` for automation and parse structured output instead of human text.
- Pass `--context <name>` when relying on an implicit current context would be ambiguous.
- Treat exit code `3` from `operations run` as a completed best-effort submission with rejected targets; report accepted and rejected targets separately.
- Use one server-side batch command for multi-client actions. Do not loop over clients to reconstruct batch behavior.
- Preserve CLI failures. Do not retry mutations with a new request identity or substitute direct API calls unless the user explicitly requests a diagnosed recovery.

Use `<cli> --help` or `<cli> <group> <command> --help` to discover the installed version's supported commands and arguments instead of assuming commands that are not present.

## Upgrade clients and components

Use `clients list` and `releases list` to identify the requested devices and eligible versions. For client previews, select exactly one of `--clients <comma-separated-device-IDs>` or `--group <group-ID>`:

- `deployments preview --scope client --all-latest` updates the selected clients' component combination.
- `deployments preview --scope client --targets <component@exact-version,...>` selects client components explicitly.
- Cross-end combinations use `--scope all --targets <component@exact-version,...>`; pure server previews use `--scope server` without selecting clients. Inspect the actual server and client impact, including required dependencies.

Keep deployment as `preview`, explicit `start`, then `wait`, retaining the preview's returned `id`. Inspect blockers, actual component versions, target devices and restart impact before starting. Do not start a preview unless the user requested the state-changing deployment; prior authorization in the session remains valid.

`deployments start --id <preview-ID> --policy independent` is the default: prepared clients switch independently, while real Service dependencies retain their required ordering. If the user chooses separate preparation and switch authorization, start with `--policy manual`, read `deployments status`, then use `deployments switch --id <same-preview-ID>` when the preparation results permit switching.

Changed client components require local user confirmation by default. The client action is "Refresh and update"; it is separate from Control's manual switch authorization. For a requested unattended test upgrade, add `--auto-confirm-core` to the **preview**, binding authorization to that frozen plan. Production rejects this option.

Use `deployments wait --id <same-ID> --timeout <seconds> --json` and interpret both its exit code and structured result:

- Exit code `0` with `outcome: deferred-offline` means the listed offline clients have not completed; do not report all clients upgraded.
- Exit code `1` means a preview error or a failed, restored, withdrawn or superseded target; inspect `deployments show` for the actual result.
- Exit code `4` with `timeout: true` means waiting timed out, not that the task was cancelled. Query `deployments status` or `deployments show`, then continue waiting on the original ID when appropriate.

Use `deployments wait --id <same-ID> --until received` to report real per-device delivery separately. `delivery[].receivedAt` is recorded only after an authenticated client reports the exact held plan/preparation or a valid receipt. Server acceptance is not delivery; offline targets remain `pending-offline`. A delivered target can later fail preparation or upgrade: read its execution phase separately. Waiting repeats only reads of the same request; it does not start another task. The default `--until completed` retains actual upgrade completion semantics.

After completion, query clients or the server overview to verify actual versions and health, then perform the requested functional checks. Cancellation is an explicit `deployments withdraw` action; stopping local waiting does not cancel the deployment.

Full installation, authentication and deployment examples are maintained in the [README CLI guide](../../../README.md#upgrade-clients-with-the-control-cli) and [CLI deployment guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md#deliver-components-with-the-control-cli).

# Teams development delivery assistant

Use the [engineering delivery map](../../../docs/development/delivery-map.md) as the entry point for the flow, so developers and Agents follow the same engineering contract. The map maintains the stages and completion conditions; the specialist guides maintain commands, parameters, input sources and troubleshooting. This Skill chooses the route, organizes execution and checks results; it does not copy the command manuals or add new gates.

## Decide the goal

First read the repository [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) and the map, then use the user's request, the current branch / worktree, any existing PR, release receipt or candidate to decide: which stage this work should reach, which components and targets are involved, and what evidence already exists or is still missing. Briefly tell the user the chosen route; do not add step-by-step approvals.

Enter the stage the task needs; do not mechanically start over from LOCAL. Whether existing verifiable results can be reused is decided by [Test gates](../../../engineering/docs/testing-gates.md). Documentation-only and similar changes follow the required plan and do not need packaging or deployment. Fixing code, packaging, deploying and merging are different operations; once the target stage is complete, do not move on to the next stage automatically.

Authorization already given in the session stays valid. When the user only asks for local development, a plan or a look at results, do not take that as permission for remote publishing, upgrades, promotion or merging; do not ask again for actions already authorized. If there is a real gap in targets or permissions, finish the checks and preparation that do not depend on it first, then state what is missing and the specific action waiting to run.

## Organize execution by stage

Read only the specialist guides and Skills this work needs. Take commands from the current guides, and before running them replace placeholders with values from source, receipts, the actual environment or private configuration; do not infer targets from example addresses or context names.

| Stage | Entry point and collaboration | Completion check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LOCAL | Follow the [development handbook](../../../engineering/docs/development-guide.md#local-startup) to prepare dependencies, PG, running from source and making changes take effect; choose the relevant self-tests and Trace verification for the change | The actual behavior and related self-tests for this change have results; remote or platform verification that was not run is stated separately |
| TEST | First use the [packaging guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md#packaging) to decide the version declaration, source and scope; if already published, verify the receipt. For installation / upgrade, use the [Control Skill](../icode-teams-control/SKILL.md) and the engineering guides it references, confirming instance identity, exact component versions and target devices | Separately check the official release receipt, the original deployment task completion receipt, the actual installed version / health and the business behavior of this change; packaging-only tasks stop at receipt verification |
| PR | Use [architecture-self-check](../architecture-self-check/SKILL.md) to cover the full candidate against the fixed merge-base with the actual base, reusing the required plan for the PR scope and valid evidence, with delivery tests listed separately via `deferredDeliveryTests`; commit, create the PR and handle CI / review feedback as authorized | The self-check report separates code and rule review, automated checks and items awaiting CI; PR creation, CI passing, review approval and merge are reported separately |
| MAIN | Follow the [main integration guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md#main-integration-workflow) and the [Control Skill](../icode-teams-control/SKILL.md#main-integration) to organize the archived component manifest, the actual server deployment and the independent client / developer business verification | Fix the production version manifest and check the actual server versions, health and configuration; run the dedicated client and developer cases separately and record the original deployment ID and results. What was not run stays not-run; new results do not fabricate historical candidate acceptance or production admission. Ordinary client rollout remains a separate manual task |
| PROD | Follow [production acceptance and promotion](../../../engineering/release/docs/release-trust.md#production-acceptance-and-promotion), [prod same-candidate deployment](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/business-deployment.md#prod-same-candidate-deployment) and the [Control Skill](../icode-teams-control/SKILL.md#production-deployment) to check evidence, promote, export the binding and deploy | Separately verify, for the same candidate, the main and full public candidate acceptance evidence, the promotion record, the actual production deployment and production business acceptance; a successful promotion only grants admission |

The Control Skill manages CLI preparation, authentication and the deployment lifecycle; this entry point does not rewrite its adaptation logic. The common self-check Skill only checks and reports; fixes remain an authorized development task. To wait for CI, use the user-level `ci-watch`. For automated PRs, check the trusted coordinator's `PR validation result`; do not treat an execution summary or workflow definition validation as final admission.

When the user specifies the TEST environment, check the actual Linux server, registry and clients against the map's [TEST environment topology and entry points](../../../docs/development/delivery-map.md#test--package-select-targets-and-verify-upgrades). `release-acceptance.yml` with `test_environment=true` only accepts Linux TEST services and native Windows clients that are already deployed; server release and deployment must each have their own receipts first. The workflow's default mode and the `release-acceptance` mode of `architecture-checks` are still isolated native regressions; do not replace the environment the user specified just because they cover packaging and installation. If access or the repository contract is blocked, report and handle that gap explicitly; do not substitute a self-built Windows registry / server. Keep the evidence for required regressions and actual TEST acceptance separate.

## Scan component changes and version bump PRs

When the user asks which components need a release, to bump versions in bulk or to generate a version bump PR, follow the [scan and version bump guide](../../../operations/applications/deployment/docs/dual-environment.md#scan-component-changes-and-submit-a-version-bump-pr) and call the existing [refresh-component-versions.ts](../../../engineering/release/refresh-component-versions.ts). It reuses the build input analysis of official packaging; do not guess component changes from directories or commit times.

Use a clean checkout identical to the latest `origin/main`. If the current development branch or worktree does not match, use a separate checkout and prepare dependencies, keeping the user's existing changes. Registry and authentication parameters follow the packaging guide and existing configuration. Use the default mode when only a scan is requested; use `--write` when asked to change local declarations; use `--pr` when asked to complete a version bump PR, following the PR stage's common self-check and validation statement checks. Do not ask again for existing authorization; a scan request by itself does not extend to pushing or creating a PR.

Check the source, release catalog, component versions and changed files, package inputs and delivery version in the report. The script increments the patch version by default; major/minor and consumer dependency ranges still need handling based on actual compatibility. Keep unchanged pending release declarations; later source changes must be compared with the source of their first main declaration, and must not be skipped just because the version has not been released. If nothing changed, stop; on failure, locate the problem along the original branch and result, and do not bump again, overwrite the remote branch or bypass checks.

When done, return the scan conclusion, version changes and the link to any PR created; describe local checks, PR CI, and automatic packaging and deployment after merge separately. Preparing the version bump PR ends here; later delivery stages proceed as the user requests.

## Keep identity and evidence continuous

When moving between stages, keep the identities relevant to this action: source SHA / PR base, release run and attempt, candidate and combination, actual targets, deployment ID and business operation evidence. After the source, candidate or target changes, re-judge whether the affected evidence is still valid; do not attach old successful results to a new candidate.

Get environments and credentials from authorized private configuration or existing contexts, and query actual identities as the guides describe. For the current environment field mapping, see the [design notes](../../../docs/specs/development-delivery-map.md#environment-naming-and-deployment-model); the target naming is not fully implemented yet, so do not rewrite purpose / environment in bulk just because the user says test. Real addresses, credentials and raw output containing them must not be written to the repository or public reports.

Waiting on the main path uses the original run / deployment ID. Failures, offline deferrals, timeouts or missing evidence are queried and handled as the guides describe. Do not automatically resend tasks, switch environments, rebuild candidates or loosen acceptance to get a success; run recovery only once there is a clear cause and authorization. Ordinary client rollout after MAIN acceptance is run explicitly by an administrator through the CLI, reusing the server's frozen batch request; reruns keep the original device set and deployment ID, and the fixed list of dedicated acceptance devices excludes personal devices. When the current candidate has no Control verification receipt, ordinary version selection is explicitly closed; do not fill in accepted by hand or fall back to an old candidate. TEST does not push in bulk automatically. MAIN checks use the full plan including the delivery scope; a green PR gate does not substitute for it. The Linux fresh-install and dual-user upgrade side paths after basic acceptance are independent of ordinary rollout; query the original side-path run and list its actual results separately. `initialized` and `no-component-change` do not mean the upgrade is verified, and the side paths do not provide prod promotion proof. MAIN `deploy=false` is a separate packaging route; `deploy=true` freezes archived component metadata and deploys. Later advances of main do not change the manifest, and reruns keep the original selection artifact. PROD keeps using the same accepted candidate; eligibility is not obtained by repackaging or version suffixes.

## Report results and next steps

Briefly state the target stage, the actions actually completed, the corresponding identities and where the evidence can be accessed. Separate passed, failed, blocked and not applicable, and point out the unverified scope. When only suggesting the next stage, give the entry point and the missing inputs; a suggestion is not authorization to execute.

Output to the current reply or a PR description you are authorized to edit. Logs and raw results are stored outside the repository or as CI artifacts according to the [documentation maintenance rules](../../../docs/README.md). When a guide and the implementation disagree, point it out; fixing the documentation stays within the development task's scope. Reusable operating contracts go back into the specialist guides; do not accumulate another set of steps or execution history in the Skill.
